data.narrative:
Diraq is a Series A quantum computing company founded by Andrew Dzurak that has raised $100M+ to date. The quantum computing sector comprises 11 total comparables: 3 public companies (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private peers including Quantinuum, IonQ, PsiQuantum, D-Wave Quantum, and SandboxAQ.

Of the two valuation methods tested, only stage-progression proved applicable. Peer-median analysis was not viable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within quantum computing—while 8 private-sector peers exist, fewer than three met narrow filtering criteria around stage and valuation tier, making sector-wide median comparison unreliable. Stage-progression applied a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A progression to the $100M total capital raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $200M.

The triangulated valuation range is $170M to $230M, with a central estimate of $200M. This range reflects a single-method analysis; the limited peer dataset presents the primary uncertainty. Any refinement would require either closer visibility into pre-Series B quantum computing rounds or broader stage-agnostic peer calibration, though the latter introduces additional noise. The $100M+ fundraising base itself signals material investor conviction, but near-term valuation movement will depend heavily on technical milestone achievement and competitive positioning within a crowded, capital-intensive sector.
